code: const uint8_t* data = fuzzer input bytes
note: Attacker-controlled raw AAC/ADTS bitstream enters the fuzzer harness; size >= 1 is required.
The first two bytes determine container type; for raw AAC/MP4 input isADTS=false, so ui_mp4_flag=1 is set in initXAACDecoder.
Decoder API and memory tables are initialized; the input buffer is allocated and the MP4 flag is configured.
The raw input bytes are copied into the decoder's input buffer for header parsing and frame decode.
The decoder parses the AudioSpecificConfig/GA header; for ELD with LDSAC extension, ldmps_present_flag is set to 1.
When ELDEXT_LDSAC is parsed from the ELD extension, the LD-MPS present flag is set, enabling the LD-MPS decode path.
All three conditions are satisfied for an LD-MPS stream, so ixheaacd_ld_mps_apply is invoked on the decoded time-domain samples.
For LD-SBR without a separate SBR path, no_ldsbr_present is true, so the LD QMF analysis filter bank is executed on the output buffer.
The QMF bank channel count is set from qmf_band_count; for a 32 kHz LD-MPS stream qmf_band_count=64, so no_channels=64.
The complex analysis QMF filter is invoked with no_channels=64 and ldsbr_present=0, passing the time-domain samples.
The analysis window is applied to produce 128 subband samples in analysis_buffer for each time slot.
The forward modulation is called with ld_mps_flag=1, passing the analysis buffer and the QMF bank with no_channels=64.
Since no_channels=64, the cos/sin modulation is called with the 32-point twiddle table and the real subband buffer.
A 128-element local buffer is declared without initialization; it will be partially written and then read, causing a use of uninitialized value.
With no_channels=64, M=32 and M_2=16; the main loop runs (M_2>>1)-1 = 7 iterations.
Each loop iteration writes 16 elements to subband_tmp via psubband_t, psubband1_t, psubband_t2, and psubband1_t2; after 7 iterations indices 0-27, 36-63, 64-91, and 100-127 are written.
The radix-4 butterfly reads subband_tmp[0..31], including uninitialized indices 28-31, propagating the uninitialized values.
The second radix-4 butterfly reads subband_tmp[64..95], including uninitialized indices 92-95, further propagating the uninitialized values.
The post-radix computation reads the fully propagated subband_tmp values, including the uninitialized entries, and writes them into the output subband buffer.
The second post-radix computation reads the uninitialized subband_tmp[92..95] values and writes them into subband[64..127], completing the memory-safety violation.
